text:
Aisha: Noticing a spike in failed GPU attaches in eu-west1 for the past 20m. kube events show mount timeouts to /dev/nvme1n1.
Tom: Any recent maintenance or driver changes?
Aisha: We pushed an nvme driver update (nvme-drivers v1.12) to a canary subset ~35m ago. Failures concentrated on nodes labeled driver=v1.12.
Vera: Sample log: `mount: timeout waiting for device /dev/nvme1n1; kernel: nvme1: completion timeout, status: 0xdead` and SMART reports media_errors incrementing.
Kai: OpsBot alert: "local-nvme tail-latency - eu-west1 - 8 hosts" :rotating_light:
OpsBot: [alert] local nvme p99 latency >350ms, background cleaner queue depth 16x normal.
Tom: Sounds like background scrub/cleanup jobs are overlapping with kernel GC cycles causing long tail latencies.
Aisha: I can confirm cleaner jobs kicked off around the same time per controller logs.
Vera: Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce cleaner batch size (janitor.batch_size=32) 2) pin affected nodes to low-priority for new GPU scheduling 3) revert driver on worst nodes.
Kai: We can change `janitor.batch_size` via rollout; will take ~2m to propagate. Also we have scheduler-policy: `prefer_region=eu-north1 for 30m` to divert new allocations.
Aisha: Diverting will increase latency for some jobs, estimate +$420/hr. Acceptable for now.
Tom: Also throttle cleaner cron for driver=v1.12 cohort: `janitor.rate_limit[driver="v1.12"]=5/s`.
Vera: Can we apply both batch_size reduction and rate_limit for a faster win?
Kai: Yes. I'll push a canary to 4 controllers first.
OpsBot: [deploy] config change detected: janitor.batch_size -> rollout started.
Aisha: After canary, p99 dropped from 380ms to 120ms on the affected nodes. Attach success rate improved to ~98%.
Tom: Good. Keep scheduler diversion for 45m. Open vendor ticket for driver interactions with cleaner path; include nvme smart logs and kernel traces.
Vera: Postmortem stub: include timeline, driver cohort list, estimator for cross-region cost, and action to add cleaner-driver compatibility tests to CI.
Aisha: Monitoring notes: watch nvme.media_errors, attach_latency_p99, janitor.queue_depth. Will update thread with vendor ticket and rollback decision. :white_check_mark:
